title: Mass extinctions
examples: What is the difference between an extinction and a mass extinction?
How do plate movements affect life on Earth?
Are there any signs that we might be having a mass extinction now?

explain.say: Today we will learn about mass extinctions on Earth.

items: Mass extinction means many species die
over a short period of time

explain.say: The first big group we look at are the five major mass extinctions.
One very famous group of creatures were the dinosaurs.
The extinction of the dinosaurs happened sixty-six million years ago.
We also look at extinction happening in the modern world today.
Think about the ocean ecosystem as a whole system.

faq.q: What is the difference between extinction and mass extinction?
faq.a: An extinction is when one species dies out. A mass extinction means many different species die out at the same time.
asks: How many species must die for it to be 'mass'?

faq.q: Did the dinosaurs really go extinct all at once?
faq.a: Scientific evidence suggests the decline was complex, involving multiple environmental stresses over time.
asks: What was the main cause of the dinosaur loss?
Was it a single asteroid impact?

faq.q: What is the main cause of extinctions today?
faq.a: The most significant modern causes are human activities like habitat destruction and pollution.
asks: What is the biggest threat to wildlife right now?

faq.q: Do the five mass extinctions all happen at the same time?
faq.a: No, they happened over hundreds of millions of years, spaced out across Earth's history.
asks: Were they all caused by impacts?
Is there a pattern to when they happen?

faq.q: How are plate tectonics related to mass extinctions?
faq.a: Plate movements can change ocean currents and climate, which stresses global ecosystems.
asks: What role do the plates play?

facts: The five major mass extinctions significantly reduced global biodiversity.
The K-T boundary event is strongly linked to the end of the non-avian dinosaurs.
Modern extinction rates are considered by some scientists to be unusually high.
Climate change and habitat loss are major drivers of current species decline.

quiz.say: If a region loses all its large predators, what is a likely immediate effect?
quiz.show: Loss of Predators → Population Boom of Prey

options.show: The population of smaller animals might increase rapidly.
options.say: The population of smaller animals might increase rapidly.

options.show: The plants will grow much taller.
options.say: The plants will grow much taller.

options.show: The entire ecosystem will collapse immediately.
options.say: The entire ecosystem will collapse immediately.

options.show: The climate will become much colder.
options.say: The climate will become much colder.

quiz.why: Without predators, prey species can reproduce and survive more easily.

wrong.1: This is tempting because herbivores might overgraze, but the effect is on the animals first.
wrong.2: This is too extreme; ecosystems are resilient, but they change slowly.
wrong.3: Predator loss does not directly control global temperature patterns.

quiz.say: Which of these events is most closely associated with the end of the non-avian dinosaurs?
quiz.why: The K-T boundary marks the geological layer associated with the dinosaur extinction.

wrong.1: This happened much earlier and affected different groups of life.
wrong.2: This event occurred before the rise of the dinosaurs.
wrong.3: While current, it is not one of the 'Big Five' fossil events.

quiz.say: If a species relies on a specific type of plant that is now gone, what is the primary threat?

options.show: It will migrate to a different continent.
options.say: It will migrate to a different continent.

options.show: It will become a generalist species.
options.say: It will become a generalist species.

options.show: It faces a high risk of extinction.
options.say: It faces a high risk of extinction.

options.show: It will quickly adapt to eat other things.
options.say: It will quickly adapt to eat other things.

quiz.why: Specialist species cannot switch to alternative food sources when their primary one disappears.

wrong.0: Migration is difficult for many species due to barriers like oceans or mountains.
wrong.1: Becoming a generalist is a long evolutionary process, not an instant fix.
wrong.3: Adaptation takes many generations, which is often too slow for rapid change.
